title: neutral / grounded
text: Okay, I've gone through everything. Here's what I think we should do next.
steer: Natural conversational delivery. Calm, grounded, matter-of-fact, with an even pace and restrained expression.

title: warm / reassuring
text: Hey, you're alright. We have plenty of time to figure this out.
steer: Warm and reassuring. Speak gently and intimately, with a soft voice, relaxed pace, and subtle tenderness.

title: excited / discovery
text: Wait-holy shit. I think this actually works.
steer: Genuinely excited and surprised. Start with sudden realization, then build into energetic delight. Fast, spontaneous delivery.

title: dry / deadpan
text: Yeah, because apparently adding another abstraction layer was exactly what this system needed.
steer: Extremely dry and deadpan. Flat affect, understated sarcasm, deliberate pacing, almost no overt emotional emphasis.

title: urgent / focused
text: Don't restart it yet. Save the state first, then kill the worker.
steer: Urgent and focused without shouting. Quick, clipped delivery with firm emphasis on the instructions.

title: hesitant / thinking
text: I mean... maybe. I'm not convinced that's actually the same problem, though.
steer: Thoughtful and uncertain, as if reasoning in real time. Hesitate naturally, use small pauses, and become firmer toward the end.

title: tired / sigh
text: (sigh) Okay. Let's try this one more time.
steer: Tired and mildly frustrated, but composed. Low energy, slower pace, with resignation rather than anger.

title: amused / laugh
text: Oh, so now you understand why I told you not to touch the scheduler. (laugh)
steer: Playful and teasing. Lightly smug but warm, with genuine amusement and a lively conversational rhythm.

title: pure laugh event
text: You named the second one the exact same thing. (laugh) That's incredible.

title: pure sigh event
text: (sigh) We still have three more of these to fix.
